final_candidates.decision_summary: C52 is the axial heme-ligating cysteine; substituting serine removes thiolate coordination, abolishing CBS catalytic activity. Verified WT residue C at position 52.
K119 forms the internal aldimine with the PLP cofactor; K119N prevents Schiff-base formation, eliminating catalysis while largely preserving fold.
R125Q is a recurrent pathogenic loss-of-function CBS mutation in homocystinuria, strongly precedent for abolished enzyme activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 targets essential cofactor coordination and established pathogenic loss-of-function sites; further rounds offer no additional resolution.

history.rationale: Cys52 coordinates the b-type heme in the N-terminal regulatory domain; replacing it with serine disrupts heme binding and destabilizes/abolishes CBS activity.
C52 coordinates the heme cofactor required for CBS activity and stability; substituting serine removes thiolate ligation, abolishing activity. This is a well-established mechanistic target.
Lys119 forms the internal aldimine with the PLP cofactor; substitution removes the catalytic Schiff-base linkage, directly eliminating enzyme activity.
K119 is the internal aldimine-forming lysine for the PLP cofactor; mutation to asparagine prevents Schiff-base formation, eliminating catalytic activity.
Ser349 is a well-known pathogenic mutation site (S349L, pyridoxine-resistant homocystinuria) that inactivates CBS by disrupting catalytic dimer contacts.
S349 sits near the active-site PLP region, but its effect on full activity loss is less certain than cofactor-ligand mutations; lower confidence.
I278T is a common pathogenic CBS missense variant causing enzyme loss of function via misfolding; plausible LOF candidate.
Structural core mutation may destabilize but not deterministically abolish catalysis; downweight.
Pathogenic variant in the CBS core domain associated with homocystinuria and loss of activity.
P422 is C-terminal regulatory-region-adjacent; disruption there affects AdoMet regulation rather than baseline catalysis, so it is unlikely to fully abolish activity.

rejection.reason: P422 is C-terminal regulatory-region-adjacent; disruption there affects AdoMet regulation rather than baseline catalysis, so it is unlikely to fully abolish activity.

history.rationale: Gly307 is a pathogenic mutation site (G307S) causing severe CBS deficiency; small-to-bulky change disrupts the active site.
G307 is in the conserved TG GTGGT active-site loop; glycine-to-serine can disrupt the catalytic loop geometry, giving moderate confidence for loss of function.
Cys272 in the active-site region contributes to proper PLP orientation; substitution reduces catalytic turnover.
C272 lies in the catalytic core but the serine substitution may not fully abolish activity; downweight relative to cofactor-site mutations.
Conserved residue near the PLP-binding site; charge-neutralizing substitution destabilizes cofactor binding and activity.

R125Q is one of the most frequent pathogenic loss-of-function CBS mutations causing homocystinuria, with strong precedent for abolishing activity; raise confidence above speculative active-site-adjacent candidates.
